title: AI Video Generation in 2026: Sora vs Runway vs Seedance vs Vidu
description: How the four leading AI video models of 2026 differ — Sora, Runway, Seedance 2.0 and Vidu — and which one fits advertising, short-form, or narrative work.

# AI Video Generation in 2026: Sora vs Runway vs Seedance vs Vidu

AI video in 2026 has split into two distinct jobs: **generating** footage that does not exist, and **directing** footage that meets a brief. The leading tools are no longer interchangeable, and picking the wrong one costs days.

This comparison covers what each model is genuinely strong at, where it breaks down, and what it costs in practice.

Explore our [[link:/category/Video|Video category]] for more tools.

---

## The Four Contenders

| Tool | Strength | Weakness | Best for |
|------|----------|----------|----------|
| [[link:/tools/16|Sora]] | Scene realism | Limited control | Concept and mood |
| [[link:/tools/9|Runway]] | Editing + generation suite | Credit cost adds up | Production workflows |
| [[link:/tools/1563|Seedance 2.0]] | Motion and camera control | Regional availability | Advertising, short drama |
| [[link:/tools/1513|Vidu]] | Subject consistency across shots | Shorter maximum length | Narrative clips |

---

## [[link:/tools/16|Sora]]: Realism First

Sora produces clips with convincing physics and lighting, which is why it remains the default for establishing a look. Give it an atmospheric description and it delivers something that reads as filmed.

Where it struggles is control. Asking for a specific camera move or a precise sequence of actions produces approximate results, and iterating on specifics burns generations.

**Use it for**: mood pieces, concept visualisation, establishing shots.
**Avoid it for**: anything with a shot list somebody else wrote.

---

## [[link:/tools/9|Runway]]: The Production Suite

[[link:/tools/9|Runway]] is the only entry here that is both a generator and an editor. That matters more than raw output quality, because real work rarely ends at the first generation.

### Why the Suite Matters

- **Generate then fix**: Remove objects, extend shots, and clean up without leaving the tool
- **Consistent workspace**: Project assets stay in one place
- **Agentic pipelines**: Describing a storyboard and receiving a shot list and assembly

The catch is credit consumption. Editing operations cost on top of generation, and a project with many revision rounds gets expensive fast.

**Use it for**: projects with revision cycles, teams already doing post-production.
**Avoid it for**: high-volume, low-margin output.

---

## [[link:/tools/1563|Seedance 2.0]]: Directable Video

[[link:/tools/1563|Seedance 2.0]] became the year's most significant video release because it addressed the actual complaint: earlier models could not hold a human figure together through a movement, and would not take camera direction.

### What Improved

- **Motion coherence**: Subjects stay intact through movement
- **Camera control**: Explicit direction over the shot, not implied framing
- **Multi-shot generation**: Sequences rather than isolated clips

This is why it moved into advertising and short drama production, where a scene that falls apart at second four is unusable regardless of how good frame one looks.

**Use it for**: marketing video, short drama, product scenes.
**Check before committing**: regional availability and commercial terms through Volcano Engine.

---

## [[link:/tools/1513|Vidu]]: Consistency Across Shots

[[link:/tools/1513|Vidu]] built its reputation on keeping a subject recognisable across shots — the problem that makes multi-scene AI video look like a slideshow of different people. The S2 release adds real-time 720p editable output and interactive avatar characters.

**Use it for**: narrative sequences with a recurring character, concept visualisation.
**Avoid it for**: long-form production.

---

## Also Worth Knowing

Three more options cover cases the big four handle poorly:

- **[[link:/tools/503|Kling AI]]**: Strong on temporally coherent, higher-quality output for advertisers
- **[[link:/tools/502|Luma Dream Machine]]**: Fast realistic generation from text or images
- **[[link:/tools/1119|Hailuo AI]]**: Competitive output at a lower cost per generation

---

## Editing Still Happens Somewhere Else

None of these models finishes a project. Generated footage lands in an editor, and for most creators that means one of:

- **[[link:/tools/51|VEED]]**: Browser editing with captions, ideal for social output
- **[[link:/tools/201|Pictory]]**: Repurposing long content into short clips
- **[[link:/tools/1534|Opus Clip]]**: Extracting short-form candidates from long recordings

Budget for this step. Generation is the cheap part; making it publishable is where the time goes.

---

## How to Choose

1. **Need a look, not a shot list?** Start with [[link:/tools/16|Sora]]
2. **Will this go through revisions?** Use [[link:/tools/9|Runway]]
3. **Have a brief with camera direction?** Use [[link:/tools/1563|Seedance 2.0]]
4. **Same character across several shots?** Use [[link:/tools/1513|Vidu]]
5. **Watching cost per clip?** Try [[link:/tools/1119|Hailuo AI]] or [[link:/tools/502|Luma Dream Machine]]

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Which AI video generator is best overall in 2026?**
No single winner. [[link:/tools/9|Runway]] is the best complete workflow, [[link:/tools/1563|Seedance 2.0]] leads on directed output, and [[link:/tools/16|Sora]] leads on realism per prompt.

**Can AI-generated video be used commercially?**
Yes, subject to each provider's licence. Terms differ substantially between tools and regions — verify before client work.

**Why does my generated video fall apart after a few seconds?**
Motion coherence is the unsolved part of the field. Models differ mainly in how long they hold together, which is why [[link:/tools/1563|Seedance 2.0]] and [[link:/tools/1513|Vidu]] gained attention.

**Do I still need video editing software?**
Yes. Every model here produces raw footage that needs cutting, captioning and audio work before publishing.
